tdbench.name: TDBench
tdbench.notes: Temporal database-derived TSQA benchmark; relevant to temporal QA methodology, but not specific to late-Qing public-health archives.

chronicles_ocr.name: Chronicles-OCR
chronicles_ocr.notes: Cross-temporal Chinese character perception benchmark with public GitHub link in the paper; useful for OCR/VLLM perception assumptions, not a late-Qing public-health corpus.

m5hisdoc.name: M5HisDoc
m5hisdoc.notes: Chinese historical document analysis benchmark; access requires manual application and non-commercial research terms, so it is a method benchmark candidate rather than directly usable project data.

mchdoc.name: MCHDoc
mchdoc.notes: CVPR 2026 benchmark for multi-carrier Chinese historical document reading; GitHub repository is public and MIT-licensed but currently appears to contain only README/LICENSE, so dataset availability remains unverified.

hipe_ocrepair_bench_2026.name: HIPE-OCRepair-Bench 2026
hipe_ocrepair_bench_2026.notes: Unified multilingual OCR post-correction benchmark for historical newspapers and printed works; not Chinese, but highly relevant for OCR post-correction evaluation, provenance metadata, and over-correction risk.

tab_vlm.name: Temporal Anachronism Benchmark for Vision-Language Models (TAB-VLM)
tab_vlm.notes: ACL paper reports 600 questions over 1,600 Indian cultural artifacts across six categories; useful as an anachronism benchmark reference, but public access is via supplementary material and needs later verification.

ancient_bench.name: Ancient-Bench
ancient_bench.notes: Official repository provides direct Hugging Face access to 2,700 annotated images spanning 1200 BCE-1911, with WYSIWYG transcription and reading-order rules. Academic research only; original institutional-image terms still apply.

ancientdoc.name: AncientDoc
ancientdoc.notes: Official README describes a CC0 dataset with five tasks from page-level OCR to knowledge/linguistic-variant QA, 14 categories, 100+ books and about 3,000 pages. It includes Qing material but has no demonstrated late-Qing public-health subset or passage-level provenance suitability; verify item-level source provenance before any reuse.

rag_eval_historical_newspapers.name: rag-eval-historical-newspapers
rag_eval_historical_newspapers.notes: Public MIT repository provides small historical-newspaper RAG evaluation scenarios with page inventories, stable Library of Congress identifiers, page URLs and PDF/JP2/XML/TXT file references; content is sourced from Chronicling America. It is English and out of the late-Qing/public-health target domain, and the actual page files are not included, so it is an engineering/provenance template rather than project corpus data.
